claim: For every field \(k\), all weight-zero Rota–Baxter operators \(P\) on \(A=k[t]/(t^3)\) are exactly \(P(1)=at+bt^2\), \(P(t)=ct^2\), \(P(t^2)=0\), with \(a(a-2c)=0\). For each finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), their number is \(q^2\) in characteristic two and \(q(2q-1)\) in odd characteristic; up to conjugation by \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb F_q}(A)\), the numbers of classes are \(q+2\) and \(q+4\), respectively. All such operators satisfy \(P^3=0\); there are precisely \(q(q-1)\) operators with \(P^2\ne0\) in odd characteristic, and none in characteristic two.

correctness.rationale: Direct basis-pair calculations force P(t²)=0, P(t)=ct², P(1)=at+bt² and a(a−2c)=0 over any field, including characteristic two. Sufficiency checks all six pairs, and explicit generator-change conjugation yields the complete orbit partition; the normal-form counts and nilpotency-index dichotomy follow. Exhaustive finite-field checker on GF(2), GF(3), GF(4) and candidate replay for GF(5) agrees with every formula.

value.rationale: The cubic unital quotient is the first one-generator nilpotent extension beyond radical-square-zero. Its new index-three weight-zero operators exist only in odd characteristic; the all-operator and automorphism-orbit counts quantify a genuine new field-characteristic boundary. The full classification is a structurally motivated moduli calculation for a natural local algebra, not an arbitrary finite slice.
